name: Chemistry
backbone_line: The backbone of this course is MIT OpenCourseWare 3.091 Introduction to Solid-State Chemistry (Fall 2018, Prof. Jeffrey Grossman) and 5.111SC Principles of Chemical Science (Fall 2014, Prof. Catherine Drennan and Dr. Elizabeth Vogel Taylor), published under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike licence. The wording of this Brief course is original to the Academy.
formula_phrase: write the actual chemical equations, electron configurations, Lewis structures, rate laws, and thermodynamic relations such as ΔG = ΔH − TΔS and ΔG° = −RT ln K
drawings: a hydrogen emission spectrum, orbital clouds, a water molecule with its bent shape, a face-centred cubic unit cell, X-rays reflecting from crystal planes, a Daniell cell with a salt bridge, a rusting steel beam, a silicon wafer, a handwritten graph with a genuine pencil-and-paper look
names_example: ENGR 505 B, MIT 3.091, MIT 5.111, Bragg's law, the Nernst equation, the Arrhenius equation
